grammar.title: Simple descriptions
grammar.explanation: Describe a familiar thing using the present copula. The form agrees with the described noun.

grammar.title: SOV and he / she
grammar.explanation: Pashto normally places the subject before the object and the conjugated verb at the end.

grammar.title: First person: I
grammar.explanation: زه means I. The present verb often ends in ـم; retain the complete attested form.

grammar.title: Informal you and joining clauses
grammar.explanation: Use ته with a familiar single friend. او connects two complete clauses.

grammar.title: Respectful and plural you
grammar.explanation: Use تاسې for a group or respectfully with an elder or teacher. Watch the corresponding verb ending.

grammar.title: We: speaker included
grammar.explanation: موږ includes the speaker. Contrast it with تاسې when addressing both sisters.

example.pashto: موږ په کور کې خبرې کوو.
example.romanisation: moong pa kor ke khabare kawoo
example.speaker: Lesson teacher

grammar.title: They: observed group
grammar.explanation: هغوی describes people outside the speaker/listener group.

example.pashto: هغوی په کور کې لوبې کوي.
example.romanisation: haghoi pa kor ke lobe kawee
example.speaker: Lesson teacher

grammar.title: Near and far demonstratives
grammar.explanation: دا points to nearby things; هغه can point to distant things. Keep noun agreement.

grammar.title: Plurals and small counts
grammar.explanation: A plural form remains the same dictionary lemma. Numbers do not add content-word quota.

grammar.title: Here, there and where
grammar.explanation: دلته means here and هلته there. Ask location with چېرته.

grammar.title: Possession: my, your and our
grammar.explanation: Keep the owner and owned object clear; respectful your differs from familiar your.

grammar.title: Practical question words
grammar.explanation: Choose the question word that fits a person, object, place, choice or quantity.

grammar.title: Adverbs in daily routines
grammar.explanation: Adverbs add time, frequency or manner. Keep the model sentence and its verb agreement.

grammar.title: Cumulative village review
grammar.explanation: Review familiar patterns in context. No new Week 2 level schedule is introduced.

1.residential: Muhammad Jan shows you his rooms, an open door, a book and fresh bread before the home handover.
1.nature: Saleha sits beside the lake with a book and picnic bread. You can see village houses across the water. Describe these familiar things.
1.business: Edris shows his shop and fresh bread, offers cold drinking water, and points out a new book at the stall.
1.school: Ms Hameed shows the classroom, its clean room and open door, a new book and cold drinking water.
